end.summary:
Named plant-eaters, meat-eaters, and animals that eat both.
Built food chains using arrows, including algae → larva → small fish → kingfisher.
Explained that plants make food using sunlight and water and begin food chains.
Predicted increases and decreases when an owl is removed, but the effect of removing snakes was not corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not completed successfully.
end.parentNote: Manav practised grouping animals by what they eat, reading food-chain arrows, and explaining why plants come first. They used the arrow direction correctly in several chains and explained the sunlight-and-water idea. One mix-up remained: removing a snake can affect frogs and other parts of the chain, not just the snake; this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask Manav to draw a three- or four-step chain and discuss what might happen if one animal is removed.
